name: Raipur–Visakhapatnam Economic Corridor

timeline.event: Breakthrough in the Keshkal ghat tunnel (October), Chhattisgarh's first highway tunnel
Several sections in final stages; NHAI is targeting completion by December

history: This new expressway is being built to give Chhattisgarh and southern Odisha a fast, direct road to Visakhapatnam and its big sea port. The current route between Raipur and Visakhapatnam winds for nearly 590 km, while the new corridor is a much straighter 464 km, expected to roughly halve the travel time. It was taken up under the Bharatmala programme as an economic corridor and numbered NH 130CD, and most construction packages were started in 2022. It runs through the hills and forests of the Bastar region and the Eastern Ghats, and includes a twin tunnel through the Keshkal ghat — the first highway tunnel in Chhattisgarh, holed through in October 2025. Building it has taken longer than planned because of forest clearances and the difficult hill terrain, so the original 2024 target slipped. As of mid-2026 it is still under construction, with the Chhattisgarh stretch furthest along and the Andhra Pradesh stretch trailing.
facts: Designated NH 130CD, one of the Bharatmala economic corridors.
Shortens the Raipur–Visakhapatnam road trip from about 590 km to about 464 km.
Expected to roughly halve the travel time, to around 7 hours.
Includes a 2.79 km twin-tube tunnel at Keshkal ghat — Chhattisgarh's first highway tunnel.
Gives central India's mining and farming belt a faster link to Visakhapatnam port.
Crosses three states: Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
Being built at a cost of about ₹20,000 crore under Bharatmala.
Runs straight through Bastar, one of the least road-connected parts of India.
significance: Chhattisgarh grows and mines a huge amount — rice, steel, coal, iron ore — but it is landlocked. This expressway gives the state a straight road to Visakhapatnam, the nearest big sea port, so goods can reach ships in hours instead of a full day. It also drops a modern highway right through the Bastar and Koraput tribal belt, which has some of the poorest road links in the country.

travelNotes: It is not open end to end yet, so you cannot drive it as one road. When it does open, NHAI expects Raipur to Visakhapatnam to take around 7 hours instead of the 10–12 hours the old route needs. Until then drivers use the two-lane NH 30 through Kanker and Jagdalpur, which is slow, winding and best not driven after dark.
futureUpgrades: The two Keshkal ghat tunnel tubes are due to open during 2026.
NHAI is targeting December 2026 for the whole 464 km corridor to open to traffic.
